by.claim: rfc-002's push-to-stage hydration mode has no freshness signal exposed to the user: T-26443 shows that when the sync source changes with auto-sync on, Argo CD immediately syncs whatever manifests already sit on the stage/sync branch path before the external promoter has moved fresh ones in. The Application shows an ordinary Synced/Healthy state throughout, so there is no stale/dirty indicator distinguishing 'deployed the intended change' from 'deployed leftover manifests from a prior environment' until the user notices the cluster is running the wrong thing.

History & Rollback's proposed flow pushes the rollback commit directly to the sync branch outside the commit server (T-27327's `git checkout / commit / push $sync_branch`). Once the signing feature in T-28239 is enabled and the target branch's SourceIntegrity policy requires verified signatures, that push lands unsigned and the git host rejects it. The Rollback button just shows a failed push with no signing-aware message and no retry path from the History and Rollback tab — the operator is stuck until someone manually finds and fixes the commit server's signing key config.
